find: For OCR Component 01 Section A, this context is essential. Part (a) asks you to compare an extract from Animal Farm with an unseen modern prose extract. Part (b) asks a broader question about the whole text.
replace: For the modern prose question, this context is essential. Part (a) asks you to compare a printed extract from Animal Farm with an unseen modern prose extract. Part (b) asks a related question on the same text.
note: F1: “Component 01” is a banned spec code that fails the house validator; the replacement states the same structure in house wording and corrects part (b) to a related question.

find: The animals are confused but lack the confidence to argue: “If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.”
replace: The animals are confused but lack the confidence to argue. Boxer ends one such argument in Chapter 7 with “If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.”
note: F3: the line is Boxer's, spoken in chapter 7, not a chorus from the animals.

expect: Which phrase does the confused animals chant under pressure?
value: Which line does Boxer use to end an argument about Snowball?
note: F3: speaker correction; the old stem was also ungrammatical.

find: replaced by a <dfn class="term" data-def="A song or anthem designed to promote loyalty to a specific leader rather than to shared ideals.">personality cult anthem</dfn>. The revolution’s ideals have been replaced by worship of the leader.
replace: replaced by a flat song about the farm itself. The true <dfn class="term" data-def="A song or anthem designed to promote loyalty to a specific leader rather than to shared ideals.">personality cult anthem</dfn> comes in Chapter 8: Minimus’s poem “Comrade Napoleon”.
note: F4: Minimus's chapter 7 song praises the farm, not Napoleon; the cult poem is the separate chapter 8 piece. The <dfn> and its definition are kept and moved to the thing they actually describe.

find: The song of liberation is replaced by a personality cult anthem.
replace: The song of liberation is replaced by a flat song about the farm.
note: F4: same error in the key fact.

expect: A new anthem praising Napoleon
value: A new anthem praising the farm
note: F4: the keyed answer was factually wrong — Minimus's replacement song praises Animal Farm, not Napoleon.

expect: 'Beasts of England' — replaced with a personality cult anthem praising him.
value: 'Beasts of England' — replaced by Minimus's new song in praise of the farm.
note: F4: the replacement song praises the farm.

find: The replacement anthem, praising Napoleon, shows how
replace: The replacement anthem, a bland song in praise of the farm, shows how
note: F4: the replacement song praises the farm, not Napoleon.

find: Napoleon replaces it with a personality cult anthem because the original song, if remembered, would expose the gap
replace: Napoleon replaces it with Minimus’s bland song about the farm because the original, if remembered, would expose the gap
note: F4: same error in the key fact.

find: Benjamin, who can read, raises the alarm: “They are taking you to your death!” But it is too late.
replace: Benjamin, who can read, raises the alarm: “They are taking Boxer to the knacker’s!” Clover chases the van, crying “They’re taking you to your death!” But it is too late.
note: F5: “They're taking you to your death!” is Clover's cry; Benjamin's line after he reads the van is “They are taking Boxer to the knacker's!”

find: Squealer announces that Boxer died peacefully in hospital, with Napoleon at his side.
replace: Squealer announces that Boxer died peacefully in hospital and claims that he himself was at the bedside.
note: F6: Squealer says “I was at his bedside at the very last”; Napoleon is not there and only speaks at the meeting days afterwards.

find: “Your lives are miserable, laborious, and short” (Old Major’s rhetoric).
replace: “Our lives are miserable, laborious, and short” (Old Major’s rhetoric).
note: F7: the quotation bank misquotes the line a student is told to memorise for a closed-text exam. Old Major includes himself: “Our lives”.

find: Check your exam board’s specimen paper for exact timings and mark weightings.
